_meta.source: Teks asli heartodex (descriptionOriginal di file data) dengan salah ketik yang jelas dibetulkan. descriptionOriginal tetap apa adanya.

mallard: It's a neat freak that often preens its feathers, and its brain can sleep with one half while staying alert with the other.
bearded-reedling: Look at these black circles around the eyes. Is it struggling with sleep issues?
eurasian-bullfinch: Black top hat, gray tailcoat, and a red vest—this bird has a real sense of style.
eurasian-wren: In many folklore and fairy tales, it triumphs over eagles with its cleverness.
pied-imperial-pigeon: With its classic black-and-white plumage, it's always poking its head around, brimming with curiosity about the world.
greater-flamingo: It's known for its long lifespan among birds, with the oldest living up to 83 years.
blue-and-yellow-macaw: A true boss who rocks a blue-and-yellow contrast outfit. With a big appetite, serious strength, and facial tattoos, it's quite the character!
long-tailed-tit: It's like a little round fluffy ball whose chirpy personality perfectly complements the quiet Blanc.
wonga-pigeon: It's said the stress of survival turned its crown feathers white ahead of time.
blue-peafowl: With such a dazzling, radiant tail display, of course it deserves to be shown off!
european-robin: A talented songbird with orange feathers on its chest, as if wearing a tiny bib.
eurasian-collared-dove: Gentle and friendly, but that doesn't mean you can mess with them!
pink-necked-green-pigeon: Wearing an orange-red bib. Could it be stained from sipping on berries?
woodchat-shrike: With its proud red locks, it considers itself a cut above other shrikes in terms of beauty.
great-tit: It's bold and lively, and it prefers warm places.
seagull: "Where are we going?" "Oh, just stopping by the wharf to grab some fries."
eurasian-nuthatch: An agile bird that loves using tree crevices as its personal food pantry.
stock-dove: It's a fashion-forward little bird wearing purple and green chokers.
eurasian-chaffinch: Don't be fooled by its gray-blue "hood"—this little bird is an energetic songbird at heart.
eurasian-wigeon: With its reddish-brown head and bright white forehead, it stands out in any crowd.
european-shag: It holds gold, silver, and bronze in bird diving. Wonder if it feels lonely at the top with no rivals.
double-barred-finch: An adorable little spirit with black-rimmed glasses, a true social butterfly... or rather, social bird.
king-eider: Its head is in blue-black, like a freshly shaven young monk.
audouins-gull: It's a very picky little bird that only eats fresh sea fish caught by itself.
red-and-green-macaw: A big fellow dressed in the three primary colors of light; though it speaks loudly, it is very gentle.
silver-throated-tit: The "Snow Fairy"—a tiny, adorable bird with surprisingly strong attack power.
eurasian-golden-oriole: With feathers as golden as starlight, it is truly a noble among birds.
ruddy-shelduck: It primarily lives in lakes. It has a competitive nature and isn't the easiest to get along with.
pine-grosbeak: Clad in unique rose-pink plumage, it's like a little spirit of the forest.
lady-amherst-pheasant: Despite its gorgeous attire, it behaves like a true hermit.
white-wagtail: Its tail wiggles during rest, so some think its genus name means "wag-tail."
regent-bowerbird: The Regent Bowerbird prefers to perch on tall pine trees. Let's hope those red spots aren't bruises from falls.
przevalskis-parrotbill: Its modest gray-white head contrasts sharply with the vivid reddish-brown feathers on its back, hinting at a mysterious personality.
smew: It's born with a naturally dashing pompadour, and it's adorably clumsy when taking off.
wallaces-fruit-dove: A little bird in golden-yellow plumage, quite particular about fruit quality.
european-bee-eater: True to its name, it is a swift and fierce hunter of bees.
brown-noddy: With a little white top hat on its head, it's the very picture of a gentle soul.
lesser-flamingo: A flamingo slightly smaller than the greater flamingo, with pink feathers that seem dreamlike and enchanting.
great-green-macaw: Shy by nature and not very fond of socializing, its cheeks are always rosy.
african-olive-pigeon: Its chest and back are covered with dense white spots—those with trypophobia should approach with caution!
yellow-bellied-flycatcher: It's a professional insect hunter. Ants, wasps, flies, caterpillars... No matter where they hide, it always finds them. Insects beware!
long-eared-owl: Its feathers help it move in silence. With large, round eyes, it acts as a skilled hunter in the darkness.
red-faced-cormorant: If you were to take off its red eye mask… better not do that!
cinnamon-ground-dove: It seems the East Pier of Fishing Village feels more like a foothill habitat to them. Living here, even the feathers on their chests seem tinted with the color of sea sand.
hawfinch: Its beak shines with a unique metallic sheen, small yet sharp.
common-kestrel: With connected white eyebrows, face readers judge it as stubborn and hard to tame.
tern: During courtship, the male presents fish he has caught to the female as a gesture of affection… Fishies, this love is in your hands now.
lears-macaw: A calm indigo plumage that highlights a gentlemanly demeanor.
azure-tit: It enjoys moving through flower fields, observing everything around it with a seemingly serious expression.
jambu-fruit-dove: Why the red-and-green combo? it looks like Xmas
peregrine-falcon: As the fastest bird in the world, its gaze radiates unrivaled pride.
eastern-bluebird: A brightly colored little bird that believes life is meant to be lived in the open wild.
pink-pigeon: With bouquet-like pink and white feathers, it hides among the flowers where no one can find it.
redpoll: Wearing a striking crimson cap and a dark mask, every appearance feels like a small fashion show.
imperial-shag: The imperial cormorant—the cormorant among cormorants, the ruler of them all.
american-flamingo: After consuming large amounts of carotenoids, it turns completely pink—truly eating its way to beauty and health.
white-headed-duck: It has a snow-white face, shining black wings, and a beak that seems to have taken a swim in a dye bath.
green-peafowl: It wears bronze-green plumage, a symbol of nobility and good fortune.
paradise-tanager: Its neon-green head shows an air of mystery, fully displaying its pride.
eagle-owl: It's charming and adorable, yet extremely shy, living deep in forests far from humans.
azores-bullfinch: No one is safe from the danger of being knocked out by its cuteness.
amur-falcon: Its feathers are all a dull gray, except for pair of red boots that catch the eye instantly.
verditer-flycatcher: Its entire body gleams in vibrant turquoise, with the eye mask serving as the perfect finishing touch.
blue-hoopoe: Its blue feathers give it a cool, distant air-like a lone ranger perched on a branch.
colorful-hoopoe: With such dazzling colors, it's got to be a hit in the mating game.
orange-hoopoe: Its bright orange crest is like a blooming crown-hard to miss. And they say if you show a hoopoe info card to a certain nature magazine, you'll get an auto-reply that just says "It's a hoopoe."
red-hoopoe: Its red crest blazes like a flame-bold and striking, as if it's about to drop some profound wisdom.
green-hoopoe: Its long, slightly curved beak is perfect for catching insects, making it a real friend to farmers and forests.
wandering-albatross: True to its name, it spends most of its life drifting over the open sea.
grey-mantled-albatross: Its feathers look like an ink painting-but the thin line near its black beak is the real masterpiece.
white-spoonbill: Dressed in nearly all-white feathers, its bright yellow neck and beak tip stand out like little flashes of sunshine.
roseate-spoonbill: The only member of the spoonbill family with soft pink feathers. Quiet, elegant, and easy on the eyes.
white-winged-tern: Cool on the outside but secretly a softie, this little water-dweller will turn into a feisty fighter the moment anyone dares to enter their territory.
pomarine-skua: Known as a "sea bandit" for stealing food from other seabirds. No wonder it got that name.
blue-brick-sparrow: Blue birds prefer open woodlands and watersides—a preference shared by this blue brick sparrow.
purple-brick-sparrow: Purple birds are incredibly rare. If you want to see one, this purple brick sparrow is probably the closest you'll get... right?
colorful-brick-sparrow: With such adorable colorful brick sparrows popping up in town, it's only a matter of time before bird facts go mainstream.
pink-brick-sparrow: Most pink birds aren't born with their rosy feathers, and the same goes for this pink brick sparrow.
green-brick-sparrow: Like many green birds, the green brick sparrow has a lighter underside—a clever trick called "countershading" to stay hidden from predators.
blue-suit-dove: A Suit Dove in a blue suit, playing the mastermind in corporate drama films.
gray-suit-dove: A Suit Dove in a gray suit, drifting like a lost passerby down gray streets.
striped-suit-dove: A Suit Dove in a striped suit, seemingly a regular in bizarre satire films.
red-suit-dove: A suit dove in a red suit is making waves among actor doves for his portrayal of a crazy, dangerous villain.
green-suit-dove: A Suit Dove in a green suit, reminiscent of a professor harboring secrets in an arthouse film.
winter-mallard: A Mallard Temperature Regulator in a winter outfit, its heavy head packed with useful data.
winter-greater-flamingo: A Flamingo-shaped Temperature Regulator whose long neck also needs to stay warm.
winter-mandarin-duck: True to its form as a Mandarin Duck, even its winter outfit is fashioned into a special heart shape.
winter-smew: A Smew Temperature Regulator in a winter outfit. It covers up that cool slicked-back look, but somehow just makes it adorkable.
winter-eurasian-wigeon: A Eurasian Wigeon Temperature Regulator in a brown winter outfit—can you even call it a "Eurasian Wigeon" now?
